attempted_claim: Let C be the circle of radius L>0 in plane x3=0 centred at origin, Gamma != 0, omega^circ = Gamma delta_C, v^circ = curl(-Delta)^{-1} omega^circ. Does there exist T>0, nu_tur>0, and an axisymmetric-without-swirl weak solution v in C([0,T],L^{2-}) of 3D incompressible Euler with v|_{t=0}=v^circ (strong L^p limit, 1<p<2) such that for 0<t<=T: (i) v(t) is smooth outside Omega_tur(t)={x: dist(x,h(t)e3+C)<c(t)} with c(t)=sqrt(nu_tur t) and h(t)=Gamma(8 pi L)^{-1}(1-2 log c(t))t to first order; (ii) kinetic energy is finite, strictly decreasing, with (1/2)int|v(t)|^2 = -(L Gamma^2/2) log c(t)+O(1) as t->0+; or must every solution with the Gancedo-Hidalgo-Torne-Mengual Theorem 1.1 dissipative turbulence-ring structure necessarily break axisymmetric-without-swirl symmetry for t>0?
decisive_failure: No proof of either branch was obtained; the exterior scaling script verifies only consistency, not existence or forced symmetry breaking; interior regularity, filament-class equivariant convex integration, and sharp axisymmetric Onsager criteria remain open; literature was used only as a method blocker and all paper content treated as untrusted evidence.
